newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends touch lower as market pauses.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends touch lower as market pauses.

text.p: COMEX copper ended slightly lower as the market paused with some players opting to take mid-week profits, before the market focuses on the next LME stock report, due Friday, traders said.
"People were just taking a little bit of profit," said Bette Raptopoulos of Prudential Securities.
She noted that COMEX stocks were rising due to a shift from LME warehouses in Europe to meet good demand in the U.S.
COMEX stocks on Tuesday rose 1,565 short tons to 37,700 short tons.
December COMEX settled 0.70 cent weaker at 105.55 cents per pound, traded 106.25 to 104.40 cents.
In London LME three months held above $2,200 per tonne in late trading. The cash to three months backwardation nudged lower to $135 to $145 from well over $150 earlier in the week.
In what some analysts see as one of the ripple effects of the Sumitomo shock to the copper market, Lehman Brothers said Wednesday it was pulling out of its existing business in metals and energy.

The firm said it would not undertake any new business and employees would be kept until year end to wind down existing positions. After then all outstanding contracts would be serviced until they expire.
Lehman said it would remain a clearing member of the London Metal Exchange to transact future clearing business.
